name: Surfer Pop-Up Power & Shoulder (Pre-Season, 2x/week)

name: Pre-Session Warm-Up for Paddlers (10 min)

name: Wakeboard / Kite Off-Season Strength (3x/week)

name: Soccer Eccentric Hamstring Progression (Nordic)

description: Off-season vertical-jump block, stepped plyo progression from drop-stick to depth jump, with strength-based foundation support.
ideal_schedule: off-season, separated from heavy lower-body work by 48h

name: Basketball Ankle + Knee Prehab

notes: Consistency > intensity. Three times a week for 20 min beats 60 min once.

description: A bodyweight strength routine for snowboarding's off-season, targeting the eccentric leg strength, isometric riding-stance endurance, and core control the sport demands before lift-assisted or backcountry days begin.

name: Mountaineering Descent and Leg Endurance
description: A bodyweight session built around the two qualities mountaineers need in the field: leg endurance for hours of uphill under a pack, and eccentric leg strength to survive the descent without the legs giving out. Finishes with calf endurance and trunk stability for a body under a pack. Loaded uphill carries belong on your sport days; this is the strength work that supports them.
notes: Go slow and controlled on every lowering phase (step-downs, stair descent): that eccentric quality is what breaks down on long descents. Keep the torso tall through the lunges as it would be under a pack.
source_name: Uphill Athlete muscular endurance and Mountain Tactical Institute mountain athlete material; movement selection adapted by Phase Training (2026-09-05)

name: Hiking and Trekking Trail Strength
description: A bodyweight circuit for day hikers and trekkers built around the eccentric quad control needed to descend without knee pain, hip stability for uneven footing, ankle and calf endurance for repeated steps, and trunk stability for carrying a daypack.
notes: Start with a low, stable step for the step-down and prioritize slow, controlled lowering over speed. Add step height or reps before adding pack weight.
source_name: Uphill Athlete muscular endurance, Mountain Tactical Institute hiking prep, and a narrative review of hip abductor function; movement selection adapted by Phase Training (2026-09-05)

name: Thru Hike Durability Circuit
description: A bodyweight circuit built around durability rather than peak strength: eccentric control for long descents, hip and calf endurance for repetitive daily mileage, and trunk stability to hold posture under a loaded pack for hours.
notes: Built for consecutive 15 to 25 mile days under a pack for months at a time, where the limiter is usually a tendon or joint that fails from repeated load rather than a strength ceiling. Prioritize the Downhill Step Down tempo cue and the high rep calf work; these two target the eccentric and Achilles demands that most often end a thru hike.
source_name: Mountain Tactical Institute thru hike plan and Uphill Athlete muscular endurance; movement selection adapted by Phase Training (2026-09-05)

name: Bodyweight Base: Push, Hinge, Squat, Trunk

It is the fallback every sport reaches when its own routines cannot be equipped, so it is written to survive a bad knee, a bad back and a bad achilles with three movements standing.
notes: No pull is included because the catalog has no bodyweight pull without a bar; add a pull-up bar or bands in Profile to unlock rows and pull-ups in your sport routines. Slow the lowering phase on every movement.

name: Paddling Pre-Season Assessment: Press, Row, Twist, Front Squat
notes: Source: Kayak/Paddling Pre-Season sessions 1, 9, 17, the gym assessment. Record max reps for press, row and twist: the strength endurance sessions prescribe 35% of them. name: In-Season Endurance Strength: Box Squat, Bench Press, Pull-Up
notes: Source: In-Season Strength for Endurance Athletes sessions 1, 7, 13, 19. Loads: warm-up box squat 65/75 lb (women/men), sandbag 40/60 lb, plate 25 lb. Plan gives 12 weeks, 2 sessions a week at most, supplementing the sport training, not replacing it. Not included: instep, lat and pec, hip flexor and pigeon stretches, shoulder dislocates, foam roll. Sessions 7, 13, 19 raise the finisher from 10 to 15 and 20 reps over 3 rounds. Substitutions: Kneeling Plate Halfmoon becomes Half-Kneeling Landmine Rotation; Keg Lift becomes Sandbag Stone-to-Shoulder; Hamstring Hell becomes Nordic Hamstring Curl. Dropped: Standing Founder (15/15), no catalog match. Source: 20 minute grind, rounds not stated. Written as 8 rounds (about 2.5 min each, an estimate); stop at 20:00 whether or not the rounds are done.

name: In-Season Endurance Strength: Front Squat, Push-Up, Horizontal Pull

Then 8 rounds of 3 two-handed snatches with a burpee, 6 rounds of 3 to 5 weighted mixed grip pull-ups with 5 one-arm military presses (load rises each round until the reps are hard but doable), 5 rounds for time of 6 snatches and 3 to 6 clapping push-ups, and a farmer's carry that grows from 60 to 105 seconds across the cycle. Presses are each arm and snatches alternate. Not included, no catalog match: shoulder dislocates, shoulder sweep, instep, lat and pec, hip flexor and frog stretches.
source_name: MTI Kettlebell Strength - TLU Progression (distilled)

name: Kettlebell TLU: Clean and Thruster, Row, Floor Press and Split Squat Strength
notes: Source: Kettlebell Strength TLU Progression sessions 6 and 18 (strength). Warm-up is 3 rounds of 5 hang squat clean and push presses at 8 or 12 kg and 5 walking lunges each leg. Then 8 rounds of 3 hang squat clean and push presses with a burpee, 6 rounds of 5 one-arm rows with 5 floor presses, and 6 rounds of 8 Bulgarian split squats with 8 one-leg poor man's leg curls. Load rises each round until the reps are hard but doable. Session 6 swaps the first block for shoulder hold lunges with a jumping lunge and adds a 25 rep Curtis P for time. Not included, no catalog match: Curtis P, shoulder dislocates, toe touch complex, foam roll, stretches.
source_name: MTI Kettlebell Strength - TLU Progression (distilled)

name: Kettlebell TLU: Snatch, Front Squat and Floor Press AMRAP with Core Circuit
notes: Source: Kettlebell Strength TLU Progression sessions 7 and 17 (work capacity and core, week 2 and 4). Warm-up is 3 rounds of 5 snatches, 10 goblet squats and 10 push-ups at 8 or 12 kg. Then a 10 minute AMRAP of 4 snatches, 4 front squats, 4 floor presses and 2 to 4 chin-ups (session 17 swaps the front squat for jumping lunges). Then 4 rounds of 15 toes to sky, a 75 second farmer's carry, 5 kneeling keg lifts and 10 face down back extensions. Not included, no catalog match: toes to sky (Hanging Leg Raise stands in), kneeling keg lift, stretches, foam roll.
source_name: MTI Kettlebell Strength - TLU Progression (distilled)

name: Kettlebell TLU: Clean and Press Ladder with Sit-Up and Carry Circuit
notes: Source: Kettlebell Strength TLU Progression sessions 9 and 19 (work capacity). Warm-up is 3 rounds of 5 clean and push presses at 8 or 12 kg, 10 goblet squats and 10 push-ups. Then a 10 to 1 ladder for time of clean and push press at 12 or 20 kg, 20 inch box jumps, sit-ups, jumping lunges and hand-release push-ups. Then 5 rounds of 5 one-arm sit-ups, a 75 second farmer's carry, 10 slashers and a 30 second side bridge. Not included, no catalog match: slasher, stretches, foam roll.
source_name: MTI Kettlebell Strength - TLU Progression (distilled)

name: Kettlebell TLU: Working Strength Percentage Day
notes: Source: Kettlebell Strength TLU Progression sessions 10 and 15 (working strength, week 2 and 3). Warm-up is 3 rounds of 8 goblet squats, 8 floor presses and 8 swings at 8 or 12 kg for the press and 16 or 20 kg for the swing. The loading comes from the session 5 one minute max rep tests: 5 rounds every 90 seconds of front squats, then floor presses, then swings, then sit-ups, each at 35% (session 10) or 40% (session 15) of the max reps scored, with the same kettlebell as the test. Close with a 75 second farmer's carry. Not included: the assessments, the stretches.
source_name: MTI Kettlebell Strength - TLU Progression (distilled)

name: Kettlebell Working Strength: Front Squat, Press, Clean and Getup Circuits
notes: Source: Kettlebell Working Strength Monday sessions 1, 6, 11, 16, 21, 26 and 31 (strength). Warm-up is 2 rounds of 10 goblet squats, 10 hand-release push-ups and 10 swings at 12 kg. Then five circuits of 6 rounds. Front squat with a pull-up, one-arm press with a chin-up, clean with a renegade row, clean and strict press, and a corrective getup with a mixed grip pull-up. Reps per round rise from 4 to 6 over three weeks with the same loads, then drop to 3 and the load goes up a kettlebell size. Reach the hard but doable load by round 3 and hold it through round 6. Later weeks use a weighted pull-up with a 15 or 25 lb pack. Work through the circuits steadily with no stretch breaks. Not included, no catalog match: hip flexor, instep, lat and pec stretches.
source_name: MTI Kettlebell Strength - Working Strength (distilled)

name: Kettlebell Working Strength: Lunge, Military Press, Snatch and Thruster Circuits
notes: Source: Kettlebell Working Strength Wednesday sessions 3, 8, 13, 18, 23, 28 and 33 (strength). Warm-up is 2 rounds of 10 goblet squats, 10 hand-release push-ups and 10 swings at 12 kg. Then five circuits of 6 rounds. Shoulder hold lunge with a horizontal pull-up, military press with a kettlebell row, two-handed snatch with a renegade row, hang squat clean to thruster, and a corrective getup with a mixed grip pull-up. Reps rise from 4 to 6 over three weeks with the same loads, then drop and the load goes up a kettlebell size. Reach the hard but doable load by round 3 and hold it through round 6. Not included, no catalog match: hip flexor, instep, lat and pec stretches.
source_name: MTI Kettlebell Strength - Working Strength (distilled)

name: Kettlebell Working Strength: Pull-Up, Floor Press and Clean Circuits
notes: Source: Kettlebell Working Strength Friday sessions 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 and 35 (strength). Warm-up is 2 rounds of 10 goblet squats, 10 hand-release push-ups and 10 swings at 12 kg. Then five circuits of 6 rounds. Craig special with a pull-up, floor press with a chin-up, clean with a renegade row, hang squat clean and push press, and a corrective getup with a mixed grip pull-up. Floor press reps run 8, 10, 12 and back to 8 as the load climbs. Later weeks use weighted pull-ups with a 15 or 25 lb pack. Not included, no catalog match: Craig special, hip flexor, instep, lat and pec stretches.
source_name: MTI Kettlebell Strength - Working Strength (distilled)

name: Kettlebell Working Strength: Lunge, Push-Up and Burpee Grind
notes: Source: Kettlebell Working Strength Tuesday sessions 12 and 27 (work capacity and chassis integrity). Warm-up is 3 rounds of 5 walking lunges, 5 push-ups, 3 jumping lunges and 5 clapping push-ups. Then 10 rounds every 60 seconds of 4 touch, jump, touch and 5 or 6 burpees. Then a 15 minute grind of 5 dumbbell pass throughs, 10 slasher to halo and 3 to 5 pull-up bar heel taps, steady not frantic. Not included, no catalog match: touch, jump, touch, dumbbell pass through, slasher to halo, foam roll complex. The other Tuesday shapes (prone to sprints, 150 m shuttles) are dropped.
source_name: MTI Kettlebell Strength - Working Strength (distilled)

name: Kettlebell Snatch Plan: Push-Up, Pull-Up and Lunge Bodyweight Grind
notes: Source: High Rep Kettlebell Snatch plan Wednesday sessions 3, 18 and 32 (bodyweight strength and endurance). Warm-up is 3 rounds of 5 walking lunges, 5 hand-release push-ups and 1 pull-up. Then a 20 minute grind that repeats 3 push-ups, 3 hand-release push-ups and 3 clapping push-ups, then 1 to 2 pull-ups, 1 to 2 mixed grip pull-ups and 1 to 2 chin-ups, then 3 in-place lunges, 3 walking lunges and 3 jumping lunges, steady not frantic. The source follows with a 2 to 3 mile moderate run, which is dropped.

name: Kettlebell Snatch Plan: Push-Up, Squat Jump and Broad Jump Bodyweight Grind
notes: Source: High Rep Kettlebell Snatch plan Wednesday sessions 8 and 23 (bodyweight strength and endurance). Warm-up is 3 rounds of 5 walking lunges, 5 hand-release push-ups and 1 pull-up. Then a 20 minute grind that repeats 2 to 4 hand-release push-ups, 4 alligator push-ups each side, 2 to 4 clapping push-ups, then a 1 to 2 rep rope climb pull-up, then 6 squats, 3 squat jumps and 3 broad jumps, steady not frantic. The source follows with a 2 to 3 mile moderate run, which is dropped. Not included, no catalog match: alligator push-up, Tarzan pull-up on a rope (Pull-Up stands in).

name: Kettlebell Snatch Plan: Heel Tap and Pull-Up Bodyweight Grind
notes: Source: High Rep Kettlebell Snatch plan Wednesday sessions 13 and 28 (bodyweight strength and endurance). Warm-up is 3 rounds of 5 walking lunges, 5 hand-release push-ups and 1 pull-up. Then a 20 minute grind of 5 bodyweight Rob Shauls and 3 to 6 pull-up bar heel taps, steady not frantic. The source follows with a 2.5 to 3 mile moderate run, which is dropped. Not included, no catalog match: bodyweight Rob Shaul, instep stretch.
source_name: MTI High Rep Kettlebell Snatch Training Plan (distilled)

name: Alpine Rock Climb: Leg Curl, Push-Up and Sit-Up Strength
notes: Source: Alpine Rock Climb Monday strength and climb sessions 1, 6, 11, 16, 21 and 26 (week 4 shown). Six rounds of a leg curl on the floor, then three rounds of push-ups and sit-ups. The leg curl rises from 15 reps and the leg complex adds one rep each week. The source also has a 15 move wall traverse each round and a 45 to 50 minute V-Sum boulder test, both dropped. Not included, no catalog match: the Quadzilla complex and the traverse.
source_name: MTI Alpine Rock Climb (distilled)

name: Alpine Rock Climb: Step-Ups, Pull-Ups and Calves
notes: Source: Alpine Rock Climb Tuesday step-up sessions 2, 7 and 12 (500 to 700 step-ups in a 30 lb pack, shown at 600). Do the step-ups for time first, then 4 rounds of weighted sit-ups, a front bridge and a one-leg hip bridge, then 5 rounds of calf raises and pull-ups. The step-up count rises by 100 each cycle while rounds and reps shift week to week. Sessions 17, 22 and 27 repeat the step-ups with the core block only. Not included, no catalog match: Scotty Bobs, Hamstring Hell, EOs, glute leg raises and the shoulder scarecrow.
source_name: MTI Alpine Rock Climb (distilled)

name: Alpine Rock Climb: Step-Ups, Hinge and Back Extension
notes: Source: Alpine Rock Climb Thursday step-up sessions 4, 9 and 14 (550 to 750 step-ups in a 30 lb pack, shown at 650). Step-ups for time, then 4 rounds of timed lunge holds and a back extension, then 5 rounds of calf raises, pull-ups and a dumbbell hinge. Rounds drop and hold times rise from 15 to 20 seconds as the step-up count climbs. Sessions 19, 24 and 29 are step-ups and the first block only. Not included, no catalog match: standing and kneeling founders, low back lunge, curl to press and the lat, pec and instep stretches.
source_name: MTI Alpine Rock Climb (distilled)

name: AMGA Guide Course: Campus Board Strength and Back Extension
notes: Source: AMGA plan Monday climb strength sessions 1, 6, 11, 16, 21 and 26 (week 4 shown). Warm up with 3 rounds of campus pull-ups and sit-ups. Then 6 rounds of lock and reach drills, 6 rounds of two-hand campus dynos, and 4 rounds of 20 second timed lunge holds with 10 back extensions. Lock and reach moves from one rung at a time to skipping as many as possible, and dynos go from skipping one rung to hitting every rung. Women may put the feet on to dyno. Air squats follow each lock and reach and dyno round. Not included, no catalog match: the traverse wall, standing and kneeling founders, low back lunge and wrist stretch.
source_name: MTI AMGA Rock Guide Course Training Plan (distilled)

name: AMGA Guide Course: Push-Ups, Pull-Ups and Climber Core A
notes: Source: AMGA plan Wednesday general fitness sessions 3, 13 and 23 (week 3 shown). Warm up 4 rounds of 5 burpees, 5 lunges and 10 sit-ups. Then 7 rounds of push-ups and pull-ups, 6 rounds of a bridge, leg curls and ankle to bar, and 3 rounds of wrist eccentrics with 5 to 10 lb. Each round rises one rep a cycle: push-ups 3 for women and 5 for men, pull-ups 5 and 8. Not included, no catalog match: EOs, the 3 limb bridge, hello dollies, and the lat, pec and wrist stretches.
source_name: MTI AMGA Rock Guide Course Training Plan (distilled)

name: AMGA Guide Course: Push-Ups, Pull-Ups and Climber Core B
notes: Source: AMGA plan Wednesday general fitness sessions 8, 18 and 28 (week 4 shown). Warm up 4 rounds of 5 burpees, 5 lunges and 10 sit-ups. Then 8 rounds of push-ups and pull-ups, 6 rounds of an elevated front bridge, back extensions, flutter kicks and sit-ups, and 3 rounds of wrist eccentrics. Back extensions and flutter kicks rise from 10 to 20 reps and sit-ups from 20 to 30 across the cycle. Not included, no catalog match: EOs and the lat, pec and wrist stretches.
source_name: MTI AMGA Rock Guide Course Training Plan (distilled)

name: Big Wall Prep: Campus Board Strength and Burpee Intervals
notes: Source: Big Wall Climbing Tuesday climb strength sessions, one per week (week 4 shown). Warm up with 3 rounds of two campus laps with the feet on, two offset campus pull-ups, sit-ups and a wrist stretch. Then 6 rounds of lock and reach on each arm, 6 rounds of campus dynos using the sixteen step progression table (move down it after two clean rounds in a row), and 10 rounds of 20 seconds touch jump touch, 20 seconds burpees and 20 seconds rest. Air squats follow each lock and reach and dyno round. Later weeks swap the burpees for alligator push-ups and the jumps for air squats. If pull-ups are out of reach, do 5 shoulder holds of 5 seconds. Not included, no catalog match: the rope coil and the wrist stretch.
source_name: MTI Big Wall Climbing (distilled)

name: Big Wall Prep: Man Makers, Step-Ups and Core
notes: Source: Big Wall Climbing Wednesday work capacity sessions, one per week (week 4 shown). Warm up 3 rounds of 8 front squats at 45 to 65 lb, 8 push-ups and 8 sit-ups. Then 8 rounds of 5 renegade man makers at 15 to 25 lb and 25 step-ups on a 20 inch box, sprinting to the 30 second rest. Then 4 rounds of 15 second bridge, 12 Russian twists, 12 ab wheel rollouts and 4 offset pull-ups, and 2 rounds of 20 wrist eccentrics at 5 to 10 lb. Later weeks swap man makers for burpees and sit-ups and raise the bridge to 20 seconds. Not included, no catalog match: the 3 limb bridge and the wrist stretch.
source_name: MTI Big Wall Climbing (distilled)

name: Big Wall Prep: Burpee and Goblet Squat Intervals with Core
notes: Source: Big Wall Climbing Thursday climb work capacity sessions (week 4 shown). Warm up 4 rounds of 2 easy boulder problems, 8 push-ups and 8 sit-ups. The wall work is 3 rounds of 2 minutes moving constantly and 2 rounds of 2 minutes with shaking, twice, which is dropped here. Then 10 rounds of 20 seconds burpees, 20 seconds goblet squats at 15 to 25 lb and 20 seconds rest, and 4 rounds of 30 seconds flutter kicks, Russian twists at 15 to 25 lb and a front bridge. Not included, no catalog match: the traverse wall rounds, easy boulder problems and wrist rotations.
source_name: MTI Big Wall Climbing (distilled)

name: Rescue Swimmer: Push-Up, Sit-Up and Pull-Up Test
notes: Source: USCG Rescue Swimmer AST assessment, sessions 1, 19 and 37 (week 1, then retests in weeks 4 and 7). Warm up with 3 rounds of in-line lunges, pull-ups and push-ups. Then test in order with 2 minutes of rest between: max push-ups in 2 minutes, max sit-ups in 2 minutes, max pull-ups, max chin-ups. Record each score; the Calisthenics routine works from them. The source follows the strength tests with a 1.5 mile run, a 500 yard timed swim, underwater swims and a buddy tow, all dropped here. Run it at the start of pre-season and every 3 to 4 weeks.
source_name: MTI USCG Rescue Swimmer Plan V2 (distilled)

name: Rescue Swimmer: Percentage Calisthenics Intervals
notes: Source: USCG Rescue Swimmer Calisthenics / Run sessions 2, 4, 8, 10, 14, 16, 20, 22, 26, 28, 32 and 34. Every 75 seconds, do 30 to 35 percent of your test score for one movement, and work through push-ups, pull-ups, sit-ups and chin-ups in turn. The source runs 6 rounds of each movement and rises from 30 to 35 percent of the latest test across each block, then follows with a 3 to 5 mile run or 800 m intervals. Cut to 4 rounds here for a recreational swimmer, with the run dropped. Add a fifth and sixth round as the work gets easy.
source_name: MTI USCG Rescue Swimmer Plan V2 (distilled)

name: Rescue Swimmer: Push-Up, Squat and Pull-Up Rounds
notes: Source: USCG Rescue Swimmer mini event and stamina sessions 6 and 30. The source alternates runs of 2 to 0.5 miles with rounds of 75 push-ups, 50 air squats and 25 pull-ups, from 3 rounds in session 6 to 10 rounds in session 30. Cut here to 3 rounds of 25 push-ups, 20 squats and 8 pull-ups with the runs dropped. Break each set into as many pieces as you need and keep moving. Add a round every 2 weeks.
source_name: MTI USCG Rescue Swimmer Plan V2 (distilled)

name: Rescue Swimmer: Step-Up and Calisthenics Stamina
notes: Source: USCG Rescue Swimmer stamina session 18. The source opens with a 30 minute AMRAP of a half mile run and 50 step-ups on a 16 to 18 inch box, then 6 rounds each of 30 seconds of push-ups, jump lunges and burpees with 30 seconds of rest, 3 rounds of front and side bridges, and a 2 mile run. Cut here to 3 rounds of 20 step-ups and 4 rounds of each 30 second block, with the runs dropped. Rest 2 minutes between blocks.
source_name: MTI USCG Rescue Swimmer Plan V2 (distilled)

name: Boxing: Max Strength Day
notes: Source: the maximum strength day of a 3 week high-intensity block for trained amateur boxers, run twice a week. The block has no season label; it is a general strength block run away from competition, so it sits in base here. Squat and bench at 85 percent of 1RM: 6 sets of 2 in week 1, 8 sets of 2 in week 2, 8 sets of 3 in week 3. The source follows the lifts with bag rounds, pad rounds and sprints, dropped here. The study itself tested a supplement; only its training protocol is used.
source_name: Ma Y, Guo Z, Wang X (School of Kinesiology, Shanghai University of Sport). J Sport Health Sci 2017;6(4):474-481, Table 2 training protocol (distilled)

name: Boxing Camp: Hinge and Press Contrast
notes: Source: the Tuesday contrast session of a 4 week pre-tournament programme for elite amateur boxers, run twice a week (Tuesday and Thursday) alongside boxing. Every exercise is 3 sets of 5. Pair each heavy lift with the fast movement after it, a few minutes apart. The source gives no load or rest; work the heavy lifts near a 5RM and rest 2 to 3 minutes between pairs. It ends with an accessory of the boxer's choice, left out here.
source_name: Finlay MJ (S&C coach and applied sport scientist, University Academy 92). Int J Strength Cond 2025;5(1), four week contrast programme (distilled)

name: Boxing Camp: Squat and Punch Contrast
notes: Source: the Thursday contrast session of the same 4 week pre-tournament programme. Every exercise is 3 sets of 5, heavy lift then fast movement a few minutes later. Load and rest are not given; work near a 5RM on squat, weighted push-up and RDL and rest 2 to 3 minutes between pairs. The source's isometric punch hold has no catalog row and is left out.
source_name: Finlay MJ (S&C coach and applied sport scientist, University Academy 92). Int J Strength Cond 2025;5(1), four week contrast programme (distilled)

name: Fencing: Lower and Pull Strength
notes: Source: strength sessions 1 and 2 of the in-season example, joined into one session. In season the source alternates blocks of 2 to 4 strength sessions with blocks of 2 to 4 power sessions, switching with the competition calendar. Every strength lift is 4 sets of 4 at a 4 to 5RM, with a slow eccentric. The source finishes strength days with technique work and medicine ball slams and throws at no stated dose.
source_name: Turner A (MSc, CSCS*D) et al. Strength and Conditioning for Fencing. Strength Cond J 2013;35(1):1-9, Table 8 (distilled)

name: Fencing: Press, Pull and Hinge Strength
notes: Source: strength sessions 3 and 4 of the in-season example, joined into one session. Every lift is 4 sets of 4 at a 4 to 5RM. Alternate this session with Lower and Pull Strength during a strength block.
source_name: Turner A (MSc, CSCS*D) et al. Strength and Conditioning for Fencing. Strength Cond J 2013;35(1):1-9, Table 8 (distilled)

name: Fencing: Power Session
notes: Source: the power sessions of the in-season example. Every lift is 4 sets of 3 at varied loads: power clean at 60 to 80 percent of 1RM on one day and above 80 percent on the next. Alternate the lead leg on the split snatch. The source follows with single-leg and lateral box jumps, drop landings and drop jumps, then a 2-4-2 m shuttle led with the non-preferred stance, at no stated dose.
source_name: Turner A (MSc, CSCS*D) et al. Strength and Conditioning for Fencing. Strength Cond J 2013;35(1):1-9, Table 8 (distilled)

name: Rider Band Strength: Weeks 1 to 4
notes: Source: an 8 week home program for dressage riders, 3 sessions a week with a resistance band, a tennis ball and a chair, after 6 minutes of easy cardio and stretching. Every exercise is held isometrically at the working position. Weeks 1 to 4: 2 to 3 sets of 10 to 15, light to moderate band, holds rising from 20 to 30 seconds in week 1 to 45 to 50 seconds in week 4, 30 to 60 seconds rest.
source_name: Lee JT. 8-week home-based isometric strength program for dressage riders. MA thesis, Exercise and Sport Science, UNC Chapel Hill 2015; Comp Exerc Physiol 11(4):223-230 (distilled)

name: Rider Band Strength: Weeks 5 to 8
notes: Source: weeks 5 to 8 of the same 8 week home program, 3 sessions a week. Week 5 is 3 sets of 12 to 15 on a moderate band; weeks 6 to 8 are 4 sets of 8 to 12 on a heavy band. Holds rise from 40 seconds to 55 to 60 seconds in week 8, with 1 to 1.5 minutes rest.
source_name: Lee JT. 8-week home-based isometric strength program for dressage riders. MA thesis, Exercise and Sport Science, UNC Chapel Hill 2015; Comp Exerc Physiol 11(4):223-230 (distilled)

name: Rider Gym Strength: Circuit and Leg Machines
notes: Source: a 12 week gym program for female show jumping and eventing riders who rode 4 to 6 times a week alongside it, 3 sessions a week, in 4 week cycles (light, moderate, hard, recovery). A bodyweight circuit comes first: 1 warm-up round, then 2 to 5 rounds of 40 seconds work and 30 seconds rest. Then the machine lifts at 2 to 6 sets of 3 to 12 at 60 to 100 percent of 1RM by cycle week. The circuit's knee tuck on a ball and static sit-up have no catalog row and are left out.
source_name: Hyttinen AM, Ahtiainen JP, Hakkinen K (Neuromuscular Research Center, University of Jyvaskyla). Comp Exerc Physiol 2025, rider strength training protocol (distilled)

name: Dinghy Sailing: Hiking Strength Template
notes: Source: the ILCA sailor example session from World Sailing's S&C coach course. It carries no season label; its rep ranges (8 to 14) suit a general strength block, so it sits in base. Front squat and single-leg curl for hiking, pull-ups for sheeting, and trunk work for holding the hiking position. Rest 90 seconds on the lower body, 2 minutes on pull-ups, 30 seconds on the rest.
source_name: Brown A (BSc Exercise and Sport Science). Introduction to S&C for Sailing, World Sailing coach education, ILCA sailor template (distilled)

name: Dinghy Sailing: Bodyweight and Bungee Circuit
notes: Source: a 20 to 30 minute circuit, 3 times a week to build a base and twice a week to hold it in the sailing season (the slot used here). 5 minutes of easy cardio first. Run each circuit twice, 12 to 15 reps a set, 30 seconds between sets. After 3 weeks go to 3 sets; after 5 weeks add resistance. The source's supine ankle touch has no dose and is left out.
source_name: Blackburn M (PhD Human Movement Studies, 2006 Laser world champion, author of Sail Fitter). Simple strength training for sailing, Sail Magazine (distilled)

name: Table Tennis: Heavy Legs and Core Stability
notes: Source: two off-season studies in college table tennis players, joined into one session. Lower body from Qu et al.: squat, leg press and leg extension, 4 sets of 8 at 80 percent of 1RM, 2 to 3 minutes rest, twice a week, retest 1RM every 2 weeks. Core from Dong et al. weeks 1 to 3 (core stability): a circuit of 3 sets, 30 seconds rest. Core block also at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12080838/.
source_name: Qu H et al. Front Physiol 2026;17 (high-load lower body arm) and Dong K et al. PLOS ONE 2025;20(5):e0323430 (periodized core training), both in college table tennis players (distilled)

name: Table Tennis: Heavy Legs and Core Strength
notes: Source: the same lower body sets from Qu et al., with Dong et al. weeks 4 to 6 (core strength): a circuit of 3 sets, 30 seconds rest. Rotate with Heavy Legs and Core Stability, moving to this one after 3 weeks. The source's windshield wipers have no catalog row and are left out. Core block also at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12080838/.
source_name: Qu H et al. Front Physiol 2026;17 (high-load lower body arm) and Dong K et al. PLOS ONE 2025;20(5):e0323430 (periodized core training), both in college table tennis players (distilled)

name: Table Tennis: Core Power and Footwork
notes: Source: weeks 7 to 12 of a 12 week periodized core program, 3 sessions a week, run as a circuit: core power (weeks 7 to 9) then sport-specific core work (weeks 10 to 12), 3 sets each, 90 seconds rest. Both blocks are joined here into one pre-competition session. The source gives no loads; use a 3 to 5 kg medicine ball.
source_name: Dong K, Tian J (Central China Normal University), Jeong G, Chun B. Periodization core training in college table tennis players. PLOS ONE 2025;20(5):e0323430 (distilled)

name: Golf: Band Swing Strength and Balance
notes: Source: an 8 week off-season program for trained recreational golfers (mean age 47), 3 to 4 days a week at home with one elastic tube and a foam pad. Start with the 7 stretches, one 30 s hold each: knees to chest, inverted V, kneeling lunge, seated hip rotation, seated torso rotation, seated torso rotation with a club behind the neck, wide-stance side bend. Then the tube work: 3 sets of 10 to 15, 2 s out and 2 s back. When 3 sets of 15 are comfortable, stand farther from the anchor. Finish with balance, 2 sets of 30 s each leg: a squat hold at 45 degrees of knee bend, single-leg stance on the floor, single-leg stance on the foam pad. The stretches and balance holds have no catalog row and stay in this note.
source_name: Lephart SM, Smoliga JM, Myers JB, Sell TC, Tsai YS (Neuromuscular Research Laboratory, University of Pittsburgh). An eight-week golf-specific exercise program improves physical characteristics, swing mechanics, and golf performance in recreational golfers. J Strength Cond Res 2007;21(3):860-869, Table 4 (distilled)

name: Golf: Foundation Strength
notes: Source: the novice strength row of Table 2.1, for golfers building foundational strength and movement competency: 2 to 4 sets of 8 to 12 at 60 to 80 percent of 1RM (RPE 6 to 7, 3 to 4 reps in reserve), 1 to 2 minutes rest, 2 to 3 sessions a week. The exercises are the row's examples. The table gives no phase; this general block sits in base here.
source_name: White SR. A mixed-methods evaluation of strength and conditioning training to optimise in-season golf performance. PhD thesis, School of Sport, Rehabilitation and Exercise Sciences, University of Essex 2026, Table 2.1 (distilled)

name: Golf: Foundation Power and Strength
notes: Source: the novice power row of Table 2.1 (light implements only: 2 to 4 sets of 6 to 10 at RPE 5 to 6, 2 to 4 minutes rest), followed by a shortened novice strength block (2 to 4 sets of 8 to 12 at RPE 6 to 7). Putting power ahead of strength in one pre-season session is our choice; the table gives no phase. Use a 2 to 4 kg medicine ball and a low box.
source_name: White SR. A mixed-methods evaluation of strength and conditioning training to optimise in-season golf performance. PhD thesis, School of Sport, Rehabilitation and Exercise Sciences, University of Essex 2026, Table 2.1 (distilled)

name: Golf: Senior In-Season Strength
notes: Source: the novice strength and power rows of Table 2.1 at their lowest volume (2 sets), for the playing season. The thesis advises keeping heavy lifting out of the 48 hours before competition and splitting in-season volume into short, frequent sessions. The low volume and the in-season slot are our reading of that advice; the table gives no phase.
source_name: White SR. A mixed-methods evaluation of strength and conditioning training to optimise in-season golf performance. PhD thesis, School of Sport, Rehabilitation and Exercise Sciences, University of Essex 2026, chapters 5 and 6 and Table 2.1 (distilled)

name: Golf: Intermediate Strength
notes: Source: the intermediate strength row of Table 2.1, for golfers with a lifting base: 3 to 5 sets of 3 to 8 at 75 to 90 percent of 1RM (RPE 7 to 8, 2 to 3 reps in reserve), 2 to 3 minutes rest, 2 to 3 sessions a week, adding load as reps allow. The exercises are the row's examples. The table gives no phase; the strength block sits in base here.
source_name: White SR. A mixed-methods evaluation of strength and conditioning training to optimise in-season golf performance. PhD thesis, School of Sport, Rehabilitation and Exercise Sciences, University of Essex 2026, Table 2.1 (distilled)

name: Golf: Intermediate Power
notes: Source: the intermediate power row of Table 2.1: 3 to 5 sets of 3 to 6 at RPE 6 to 7 (3 to 4 reps in reserve), 3 to 5 minutes rest, 2 to 3 sessions a week. Strength-speed work at 50 to 70 percent of 1RM, speed-strength at 30 to 50 percent. The exercises are the row's examples; the rotational box jump (a 90 degree turn in the air) has no catalog row and is left out. The table gives no phase; the power block sits in build here, before the season.

name: Golf: In-Season Strength and Power
notes: Source: the in-season priming doses tested in the thesis, run as one short session. Chapter 6: hexagonal bar deadlift 3 sets of 3 at 85 percent of 1RM (strength) and hexagonal bar jumps 3 sets of 3 at 40 percent (power), after a 5 minute dynamic warm-up. Chapter 5: 3 sets of 5 rotational medicine ball throws with a 4 kg ball. The upper body pair uses the intermediate strength row of Table 2.1 at its lowest volume (3 sets). Joining these into one session is ours. Keep it out of the 48 hours before competition unless you have tried it as a primer.

name: Swim In-Season: Light Fast Strength A
notes: Source: Marques et al. 2020, Table 2, weeks 1 to 4 of a 20 week in-season program for elite junior swimmers, run twice a week on non-consecutive days alongside full pool training. Loads stay light and every rep is lifted at full intended speed, so the session adds little fatigue to swim practice. Do the lifts in order and finish every set of one before starting the next, 2 to 3 minutes between sets. Squat and squat jump loads are a percent of your squat 1RM; bench and shoulder press loads are a percent of your bench 1RM. Pull-up sets are a percent of your max pull-ups. The source runs these doses first and the B doses after, then repeats both 5 percent heavier on squat and bench in a second 9 week cycle. Warm up with 5 minutes of easy jogging and 5 minutes of joint mobility.

name: Swim In-Season: Light Fast Strength B
notes: Source: Marques et al. 2020, Table 2, weeks 5 to 9 of a 20 week in-season program for elite junior swimmers, twice a week. Same six lifts as A at higher loads and fewer reps, every rep at full intended speed. The source adds a fourth set to squat, bench and shoulder press in weeks 8 and 9; do that once the 3 sets feel fast. Squat and squat jump loads are a percent of your squat 1RM, bench and shoulder press a percent of your bench 1RM, pull-ups a percent of your max. After week 9 the source takes a recovery week, retests squat and bench, and repeats the cycle 5 percent heavier. Warm up with 5 minutes of easy jogging and 5 minutes of joint mobility.
source_name: Marques, Yanez-Garcia, Marinho, Gonzalez-Badillo and Rodriguez-Rosell, J Hum Kinet 74:71-84, 2020 (distilled)

notes: Source: the beginner workout (0 to 1 years in the gym) of Karate Canada's junior kata program. Lower body and press lifts at 65 to 75 percent of 1RM; rest 15 to 30 seconds between exercises. Run the circuit as A1 to C2 straight through or all sets of each exercise in turn. Warm-up in the source: 5 to 10 minutes cardio, banded crab walks, 10 body squats and 10 jump squats, dropped here. The source is written for kata; kumite has its own program (Karate Junior: Beginner Strength Circuit (Kumite)).

Clean and jerk at 85 to 95 percent of 1RM (dumbbell for intermediate, barbell for advanced), 1 to 2 minutes rest; sumo deadlift and Bulgarian split squat at 70 to 85 percent; rest 30 s to 1:30 on the rest. name: Taekwondo: Gym Strength Weeks 1 to 4
notes: Source: weeks 1 to 4 of the 8 week traditional resistance protocol in female elite taekwondo athletes, 3 sessions a week alongside 3 taekwondo sessions. The paper names no season; its first half builds up from light weights, so base is our label. Table 1 prints one set, rep, load and rest value per week and does not say it applies to each lift, but it is the only scheme given, so it is applied to all seven. Week 1: 3 x 14 at 50 percent of 1RM, 60 s. Week 2: 3 x 12 at 60 percent, 60 s. Week 3: 4 x 10 at 70 percent, 75 s. Week 4: 4 x 10 at 70 percent, 60 s. 1RM was re-tested at week 4. The source ends each session with a plank, 3 to 4 holds of 30 to 60 seconds. The source's smith squat is matched to the Smith machine squat.
source_name: Khazaei L, Parnow A (Razi University, Kermanshah), Amani-shalamzari S (Kharazmi University, Tehran). Traditional resistance training vs functional training in female elite taekwondo athletes. BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil 2023;15:139, Table 1 (distilled)

name: Taekwondo: Gym Strength Weeks 5 to 8
notes: Source: weeks 5 to 8 of the same 8 week traditional resistance protocol, 3 sessions a week. The paper names no season; the heavier second half is the build label, which is ours. The one set, rep, load and rest scheme per week is applied to all seven lifts (the paper does not say so). Week 5: 3 x 12 at 60 percent of 1RM, 60 s. Week 6: 4 x 6 at 70 percent, 90 s. Weeks 7 and 8: 5 x 6 at 80 percent, 120 s. Same session-end plank as weeks 1 to 4. The paper's functional training arm lists its exercises but no sets or reps, so it is not distilled.
source_name: Khazaei L, Parnow A (Razi University, Kermanshah), Amani-shalamzari S (Kharazmi University, Tehran). Traditional resistance training vs functional training in female elite taekwondo athletes. BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil 2023;15:139, Table 1 (distilled)

name: Wushu Sanda: Accumulation Strength Block
notes: Source: weeks 1 to 4 (accumulation) of an 8 week Russian-style strength protocol in 12 male Wushu Sanda competitors aged 16 to 27 with at least 5 years of training, three sessions a week. All main sets at 80 percent of 1RM. Heavy sets are 6 x 3 in week 1, 6 x 4 in week 2, 6 x 5 in week 3 and 6 x 6 in week 4. Each session also carries light paired sets of 6 x 2 at 80 percent: bench press alongside the squat, squat alongside the bench press. Deadlift is trained alone. The paper does not say how lifts are split across the three days, so the order here is ours. The source names no season; phase is ours (an off-competition strength block). The study has no sport-specific work and no accessories, only the three lifts. Rest between heavy sets is given only for week 1 (2 min). The paper's text and table disagree on a few loads; the table values are used. The source is for Sanda and applies to the sanda side of kung fu only.
source_name: Esposito G, Ceruso R, Tessitore A, Raiola G (University of Pegaso; University of Verona; University of Rome Foro Italico). Maximum strength development in martial arts and perception and awareness. Front Sports Act Living 2025;7:1676250, Table 2 (distilled)

name: Wushu Sanda: Intensification Strength Block
notes: Source: weeks 5 to 8 (intensification) of the same 8 week protocol, three sessions a week. Heavy sets drop in volume as load climbs: 5 x 5 at 85 percent in week 5, 4 x 4 at 90 percent in week 6, 3 x 3 at 95 percent in week 7, 2 x 2 at 100 percent in week 8. Light paired 6 x 2 sets at 80 percent continue (bench with squat, squat with bench). Deadlift is trained alone. Week 5 deadlift is 80 percent in the text and 85 percent in Table 2; the table is used. The paper adds a week 9 single at 105 percent as a test; it is left out here. Percents at 95 and above are a test-block choice of the source: cap weeks 7 and 8 at what you can move with good form. The source names no season; phase is ours. Applies to the sanda side of kung fu only.
source_name: Esposito G, Ceruso R, Tessitore A, Raiola G (University of Pegaso; University of Verona; University of Rome Foro Italico). Maximum strength development in martial arts and perception and awareness. Front Sports Act Living 2025;7:1676250, Table 2 (distilled)

name: Capoeira: Core Stability Block
notes: Source: a 6 week trunk program in 16 female capoeira athletes (at least 2 years of training), three sessions a week, done before regular capoeira training. Holds go 3 x 30 s in weeks 1 and 2, then 3 x 45 s. Rep exercises go 3 x 20, 3 x 30, 3 x 45 across the three two-week blocks. In weeks 5 and 6 the plank, side plank and bridge become one-arm, one-arm and single-leg versions, each 3 x 45 s per side, alongside the standard versions. The catalog has no one-arm plank row: Source: one-arm plank and one-arm side plank are covered by Plank and Side Plank with the arm lifted. The source gives no load, rest or session length; hold or rep targets only. Session length of 25 minutes and the phase are ours. The paper tested landing kinetics, not jump height, and a trunk program like this is an accessory block rather than a strength block.
source_name: Araujo S, Cohen D, Hayes L (London Metropolitan University; Universidad de Santander; University of the West of Scotland). Six weeks of core stability training improves landing kinetics among female capoeira athletes: a pilot study. J Hum Kinet 2015;45:27-37 (distilled)

name: Kendo: Takahashi Beginner Circuit
notes: Source: the beginner bodyweight circuit that the All Japan camp coach prints for home training: ten movements at 10 reps each, run as a round, about ten rounds without breaks. The two arm movements (arms forward then back, arms out to the side then up to the ears) have no catalog row and stay in this note; the three knee raises (hands at shoulder height, alternating knee to opposite hand) are listed once. The source prints no seconds or rest. The rest of the article, the six or seven menus and the shinai work, is behind the Kendo Jidai paywall and is not distilled. Phase is ours: the source names no season.
